## Part 1: On paper

::: {#exr-geometric}
## The geometric series

1. Show that, for $q \neq 1$,
   $$
     \sum_{k=0}^{n} q^k = \frac{1 - q^{n+1}}{1 - q}.
   $$

1. Compute the value of $0.999\ldots = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 9 \cdot 10^{-k}$.
:::

## Part 2: In Julia

Download the [work files](02-convergence-series-exercises.zip) and unzip them into your project folder. Develop your code in the notebook first. Once a function works, move it into the folder `src/` and include it from there.

```{julia}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
include("src/partial_sums.jl")
```

::: {#exr-alternating}
## The alternating harmonic series

The alternating harmonic series converges to $\ln 2$:
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} = 1 - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} - \ldots = \ln 2.
$$

### Implementation

Implement the function `partial_sums(n)`, which returns the vector of the partial sums $s_1, \ldots, s_n$.

### Errors

Compute the errors of $s_{10}$, $s_{100}$ and $s_{1000}$. How many terms are needed for one more correct digit? Compare with the geometric series from @exr-geometric.
:::
